chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever performs Ziyarah and sleeps on the road, if he spends the night in Mecca, he owes a blood-offering (dam); and if he has already left it, there is no penalty upon him; and if he arrives before Mina, [penalty applies]. And that which indicates that the preferable course is not to leave [Mecca] except after dawn, is according to what we have mentioned.

key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: Dawn, the time for the Fajr prayer
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood-offering (a type of sacrificial animal or its value given as expiation)
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca where pilgrims spend the nights of Tashriq

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who sleeps on the road during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the geographical boundary for the penalty of *dam* (blood-offering) for sleeping on the road, distinguishing between those still within the precincts of Mecca and those who have exited it. It reflects the juristic emphasis on the sanctity of the holy city's boundaries during Hajj rituals. The recommendation to depart after dawn aligns with the prophetic tradition of beginning major rites at the optimal time, ensuring pilgrims are alert and prepared for the journey to Mina.
